group: PSI Score: Pneumonia Severity Index for CAP
question:
Patient note:
A 70-year-old woman who resides in her own bungalow and still gardens most mornings was brought to the emergency department by her husband shortly after lunchtime because of forty-eight hours of feverish chills, a productive cough yielding yellow-green sputum, and new right-sided chest discomfort that worsened whenever she tried to lie flat; she deliberately skipped her usual morning prescriptions—carvedilol, low-dose bumetanide, and nadolol prescribed for portal-related variceal prophylaxis—so that, in her words, “the numbers won’t be watered down.” She had eaten only dry toast at dawn and drank no coffee, alcohol, or acetaminophen before arrival, and she used neither her home incentive spirometer nor the salbutamol metered-dose inhaler she keeps for occasional winter wheeze. Past medical background includes longstanding congestive pump dysfunction following an anthracycline-based chemotherapy course in early adulthood for Hodgkin disease (she has had no malignant recurrence and has routine oncology surveillance that remains clear) and biopsy-confirmed non-alcoholic steatohepatitis with compensated portal hypertension; her last hepatology clinic visit three months earlier documented normal synthetic markers, occasional esophageal varices managed endoscopically, and no ascites. She has never required renal replacement therapy and her primary-care records show an estimated glomerular filtration rate consistently above 60 mL/min; she denies any history of stroke, transient neurologic events, carotid surgery, or focal deficits. Immunizations are current, including both pneumococcal formulations and this season’s influenza injection, and she quit a fifteen-pack-year cigarette habit nearly two decades ago. On ambulance roll-in she sat upright, conversed in full sentences, correctly recited the date and the names of her three grandchildren, and followed multi-step commands without hesitation. Skin was warm and lightly diaphoretic, sclerae were anicteric, and nail beds were pink with brisk capillary refill. First-pass, untreated vital signs obtained while she breathed ambient air at this sea-level facility were: oral temperature 38.05 °C, regular radial pulse 75 beats per minute confirmed on telemetry, non-invasive right-arm blood pressure 103/61 mm Hg verified manually, respiratory rate counted over a full minute at 20 breaths per minute with mild intercostal effort but no accessory muscle use, and fingertip pulse oximetry varying between 93 % and 94 %. Jugular venous contour was mildly elevated at the angle of Louis, similar to her cardiology baseline, and trace bilateral ankle edema was noted. Cardiac auscultation revealed an S3 gallop already documented in previous notes as well as crisp S1 and S2 without new murmurs or rubs. Pulmonary examination demonstrated dullness to percussion and absent breath sounds over the dependent half of the right posterior hemithorax with coarse inspiratory crackles and egophony just above that zone; the left lung transmitted vesicular airflow throughout. Abdomen was soft, non-tender, and mildly distended; a smooth liver edge was palpable 2 cm below the costal margin and no splenomegaly was appreciated. A focused neurologic screen showed equal, reactive pupils, intact extra-ocular movements, fluent speech, and 5/5 strength in all extremities. Capillary glucose checked immediately prior to phlebotomy read 93 mg/dL. Within ten minutes of bay entry—before any fluids, antimicrobials, vasodilators, or supplemental oxygen—peripheral venous blood and a right radial arterial sample were drawn. The basic metabolic panel returned sodium 140 mEq/L, potassium 4.2 mEq/L, chloride 104 mEq/L, bicarbonate 23 mEq/L, blood urea nitrogen 30 mg/dL, and creatinine 0.9 mg/dL. A complete blood count demonstrated leukocytes 15.1 × 10⁹/L with 88 % segmented neutrophils, hematocrit 33 %, hemoglobin 11.2 g/dL, and platelets 189 × 10⁹/L. Arterial blood gas on room air revealed pH 7.36, PaCO₂ 37 mm Hg, PaO₂ 86 mm Hg, and calculated bicarbonate 21 mEq/L, consistent with mild hypoxemia and near-physiologic acid–base balance. Serum lactate was 1.7 mmol/L, and high-sensitivity troponin I fell below the analytical threshold. A portable postero-anterior chest radiograph obtained before any therapy demonstrated a dense consolidation within the posterior segment of the right lower lobe accompanied by a crescentic fluid collection layering laterally that blunted the ipsilateral costophrenic angle; cardiac silhouette matched prior films and there was cephalization of pulmonary vasculature similar to previous images. Electrocardiography displayed sinus rhythm at 74 beats per minute with low-voltage QRS complexes and nonspecific ST-T changes unchanged from tracings in her cardiology file. Two sets of peripheral blood cultures, a nurse-assisted expectorated sputum sample for Gram stain and culture, urinary antigens for Streptococcus pneumoniae and Legionella pneumophila, and a multiplex respiratory viral PCR panel were dispatched to the laboratory prior to any antibiotic, diuretic, vasodilator, bronchodilator, corticosteroid, or oxygen order. Up to the moment this narrative is completed she has received only the minimal heparinized saline needed to maintain patency of one 18-gauge peripheral catheter, ensuring that every physiologic observation, laboratory value, and imaging finding reported above represents her untreated state at presentation.

Question: What is the patient's Pneumonia Severity Index (PSI)? You should use the patient's medical values and health status when they were first admitted to the hospital prior to any treatment.
solution:
Apply the Pneumonia Severity Index (PSI) to the untreated admission findings.
- Demographics: for a woman, use age minus 10: 70 − 10 = 60. She lives at home, so nursing-home residence adds 0.
- Comorbidities: chronic liver disease with portal hypertension → 20; congestive heart failure → 10. Remote Hodgkin disease in remission does not qualify as active or recent neoplastic disease → 0. No cerebrovascular or chronic renal disease → 0 each.
- Examination: alert (no altered mental status), respiratory rate 20 (<30/min), systolic pressure 103 (not <90 mmHg), temperature 38.05°C (neither <35 nor ≥40°C), and pulse 75 (<125/min) → 0 each.
- Laboratory findings: BUN 30 mg/dL meets the ≥30 threshold → 20. Arterial pH 7.36 (not <7.35), sodium 140 (not <130 mEq/L), glucose 93 (<250 mg/dL), and hematocrit 33% (not <30%) → 0 each. Room-air PaO₂ 86 mmHg and saturation 93–94% meet neither oxygenation cutoff (PaO₂ <60 or saturation <90%) → 0.
- Imaging: layering pleural fluid with costophrenic angle blunting indicates pleural effusion → 10.
Sum: 60 + 20 + 10 + 20 + 10 = 120.
Final answer: 120
